text.p: Belgian broker KB Securities said on Monday it advised shareholders to reduce their positions in chemical firm Solvay despite better than expected first half 1997 results.

"Even if a short-term outperformance to 23,050 francs is possible we believe that the further scope to outperform the Bel-20 index within the next 12 months is limited. We therefore recommend investors to reduce a stake at levels around 22,800 to 23,000 francs," KB Securities said in a research note.
At 0940 GMT Solvay shares were trading at 21,100 francs, unchanged from Friday's close.
The share had earlier slipped to 20,600 francs as the whole market dropped following Wall Street's decline on Friday and due to the easier dollar and fears of a German interest rate rise.
KB Securities said Solvay's above-expectations first half figures had primarily been due to much lower interest charges and good results from its Asian PVC producer Vinythai.
However, it also noted that prices in Solvay's primary markets of peroxygen and caustic soda were depressed and therefore holding back earnings growth relative to other leading chemical producers.
